verdict.summary: You can create a HubSpot OAuth app and install it in your own or test accounts in under an hour, with no review. The catch is that a Marketplace-distributed app is capped at 25 installs until HubSpot approves a Marketplace listing. A listing needs at least 3 active installs from unaffiliated customers plus complete listing pages, and HubSpot reviews it by hand.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to build a working app; 1-2 days of listing prep (docs, privacy/ToS pages, scope trimming) for the Marketplace
verdict.approval_wait: None for up to 25 installs. Marketplace listing: HubSpot promises a first review within 10 business days, and the full review cycle can run up to 60 days (one third-party guide reports 2-4 weeks)

gates.name: Developer test account / own account install
gates.unlocks: You can install the app in your developer test account or your own standard HubSpot account and connect it through Composio.
limits: The install screen warns that the app is unverified, and you must tick a box to authorize installing it
The installing user must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permissions
A community report says developer accounts created after March 11, 2026 could not create public apps during a temporary restriction. Current status is unverified

gates.name: Unlisted Marketplace-distributed app (or privately distributed app)
gates.unlocks: Real customers can install the app before it is listed on the Marketplace.
limits: Apps distributed through the Marketplace: capped at 25 installs until a Marketplace listing is approved
Privately distributed apps: up to 10 customer accounts by default, or 100 if the app was created in a Solutions Partner account
Community staff said HubSpot cannot make exceptions to install limits
Private apps get 100 requests per 10 seconds on Free/Starter accounts and 190 on Professional/Enterprise, plus a shared daily cap

gates.name: HubSpot Marketplace listing (optional later step: certification)
gates.unlocks: Approval removes the 25-install cap, so any HubSpot account can install the app and it appears on the HubSpot Marketplace.
limits: You can have only one app under review at a time. A second submission is automatically rejected
Marketplace apps get 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account (the certification page says 100)
Certification is optional and separate. It requires 6+ months listed, 60+ active installs, a security assessment and a demo video
gates.time_to_reach: Days of prep, plus time to collect 3 unaffiliated active installs, plus a review that starts within 10 business days and can run up to 60 days

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot developer account at developers.hubspot.com. Create a developer test account too, so you have somewhere to test installs.
gotchas: A July 2026 community post says developer accounts created after March 11, 2026 could not create or fully configure public apps during a temporary security restriction. If app creation fails, check HubSpot Community or contact support.

steps.title: Install the HubSpot CLI and authenticate
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI. Run `hs account auth` and connect it to your developer account; this step needs your login.

steps.title: Create the app project with OAuth
steps.detail: Run `hs project create`. When asked how the app is distributed, choose the HubSpot Marketplace if you ever want more than a handful of customers. When asked about authentication, choose OAuth rather than a static token.
gotchas: Marketplace-distributed apps are capped at 25 installs until listed. Privately distributed apps are capped at 10 accounts, or 100 in a Solutions Partner account.
A Marketplace listing requires OAuth as the only authorization method.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the `auth` block of app-hsmeta.json, add the Composio callback to `redirectUrls`. List scopes under `requiredScopes`, `optionalScopes` and `conditionallyRequiredScopes`. Request only the scopes your agent actually uses; Composio's default list is long and includes legacy scopes such as tickets, timeline, e-commerce and accounting.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URLs must use https and a domain name, not an IP address. Plain http is allowed only for localhost.
Every scope marked as required must also appear in the authorize request's scope parameter, or the authorization page shows an error.
Optional scopes are dropped silently when the installing account doesn't have that tool.

steps.title: Upload the project
steps.detail: Run `hs project upload` to deploy the app configuration. Run it again whenever you change scopes or redirect URLs.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials into Composio
steps.detail: In HubSpot, open the project's Auth tab and copy the Client ID and Client secret under Client credentials. Paste them into a custom HubSpot auth config in Composio, using the same scopes you declared in app-hsmeta.json.
gotchas: Before registering, check that the callback URL in your Composio auth config matches what you put in redirectUrls. Composio's catalog lists a different default redirect.

steps.title: Run a test install
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection and authorize the app in your developer test account or your own account. Tick the box that authorizes installing an unverified app. Then make a test API call.
gotchas: The installing user must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access permissions.
Authorization codes are single-use and expire quickly. A late exchange shows up as AUTHORIZATION_CODE_EXPIRY in the install logs.
An invalid client_id doesn't send an OAuth error back to your redirect; HubSpot shows the error on its own page.

steps.title: Check token refresh
steps.detail: Tokens come from /oauth/v3/token, using grant_type authorization_code for the first exchange and refresh_token for renewals. Refresh based on the expires_in value. Don't wait for a 401 to trigger a refresh.

steps.title: Onboard beta customers and reach 3 unaffiliated installs
steps.detail: Send your install link to early customers. A Marketplace listing needs at least 3 active, unique installs in production accounts that aren't affiliated with your organization, counted over the past 30 days. You must reach this while under the 25-install cap.
gotchas: HubSpot will not raise the 25-install cap for unlisted apps.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing materials
steps.detail: Draft setup documentation, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages, a shared-data disclosure and accurate pricing, all on live public URLs. Remove every scope the app doesn't use, and make scopes that only some users need optional or conditional.
gotchas: If any listing field is incomplete, HubSpot sets the listing to Draft.
Classic CRM cards aren't allowed in listed apps. AI connector apps must require user-level permissions or use HubSpot's MCP server.

steps.title: Accept the partner agreement and submit the listing
steps.detail: Accept the Technology Partner Program Agreement and confirm that your app doesn't serve HubSpot's restricted industries exclusively. Then submit the listing for review. Listing is free and HubSpot takes no revenue share.
gotchas: You can have only one app under review at a time. A second submission is automatically rejected.

steps.title: Wait for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing by hand. HubSpot states a first review within 10 business days and caps the feedback cycle at 60 days. Once the listing is approved, the 25-install cap is removed.
steps.est_time: 10 business days to 60 days (2-4 weeks reported)

steps.title: Optional: request sensitive-data scopes or certification
steps.detail: Sensitive-data scopes are available only to technology partners who already have a listed app. You request them through the Marketplace App Approval Request form. Certification is a separate, optional step: it needs 6+ months on the Marketplace, 60+ active installs, a HubSpot-verified domain, a security questionnaire and a demo video.

scopes.effect: Declared in requiredScopes or optionalScopes. The Marketplace review rejects listings that request scopes the app doesn't use, so request only the objects your agent works with.

scopes.scope: Legacy scopes (tickets, timeline, e-commerce, accounting, content, etc.)
scopes.effect: These are in Composio's default list. HubSpot is migrating legacy scopes to granular ones. Leave them out of a new app unless you need them, and drop any that are unused before submitting to the Marketplace.

Available only to technology partners who already have a listed public app. You request them through the Marketplace App Approval Request. Ecosystem Quality may cut back the scopes and review your security posture, and approved scopes are first allowlisted on a development or staging app. App cards must not use them, and sensitive properties can't be created, updated or deleted through the API.
Optional scopes are dropped when the installing account lacks the tool. Required scopes must also appear in the authorize URL's scope parameter, or the authorization page shows an error.

blockers.symptom: Installs stop at 25 and customers can't install the app
blockers.cause: Apps on developer platform 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs until they are listed on the Marketplace. Privately distributed apps are capped at 10 accounts, or 100 in a Solutions Partner account.
blockers.fix: Get the Marketplace listing approved, which removes the cap. Plan for this early, because HubSpot staff said they can't make exceptions.

blockers.symptom: Migrating a legacy public app with more than 25 installs fails or enforces the cap
blockers.cause: Migration applies the install limit automatically.
blockers.fix: Get the app listed before migrating, or time the migration around listing approval.

blockers.symptom: A new developer account can't create or configure a public app
blockers.cause: A temporary security restriction applied to developer accounts created after March 11, 2026 (community report; current status unverified).
blockers.fix: Check HubSpot Community or contact HubSpot support, or use an older developer account.

blockers.symptom: The authorization page shows an error during install
blockers.cause: A scope marked as required in the app settings is missing from the scope parameter of the authorize URL.
blockers.fix: Make the scopes in Composio's auth config match requiredScopes in app-hsmeta.json exactly.

blockers.symptom: Install fails with AUTHORIZATION_CODE_EXPIRY in the install logs
blockers.cause: The single-use authorization code was exchanged too late.

blockers.symptom: The listing is rejected or stays in Draft
blockers.cause: Unused scopes, incomplete listing fields or pricing, fewer than 3 unaffiliated installs, or a second app submitted while another is under review.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes, complete every listing field, confirm the install count, and submit one app at a time.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is fine for prototyping and internal use. Register your own app when you need your own client ID and secret, your own branding or redirect, a smaller scope set, or a Marketplace listing. Your own app is capped at 25 installs until its Marketplace listing is approved, so plan to list it before you scale. When you register, trim Composio's long default scope list, which includes legacy scopes such as accounting, e-commerce, tickets and timeline. Also check the exact callback URL in your Composio auth config: the catalog default (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) may differ.

open_questions: Is the March 2026 restriction on public app creation for new developer accounts still in effect as of 2026-10-29?
Does HubSpot OAuth support PKCE? This wasn't verified.
Access token and refresh token lifetimes weren't found; the docs only say expires_in is returned.
Which callback URL applies: Composio's catalog default (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) or the callback seen in the authorize probe? Check your auth config.
The per-account rate limit for Marketplace apps conflicts between the docs (110 vs. 100 requests per 10 seconds).
HubSpot doesn't state how long approval for sensitive-data scopes takes.
The developer portal's app-creation UI wasn't walked end to end. These steps rely on the CLI and project docs.
An unofficial source claims HubSpot disabled legacy private app creation on 2026-10-26. This isn't confirmed by HubSpot.
